title: Google Suspends AI Image Generation Feature in Google Earth: Strengthening Security Measures Within 48 Hours of Launch

content_html:
Google announced the suspension of a newly launched AI image generation feature in Google Earth. The feature was temporarily shut down less than 48 hours after its launch due to potential risks of misinformation. The official stated that further security measures will be strengthened. Previously, Google integrated the image generation model Nano Banana2 into Google Earth, allowing users to generate fictional scenes on real satellite images, aerial photographs, and 3D maps through text instructions.

According to a test by the BBC, the feature can generate fake scenes including "the collapse of the Eiffel Tower," "a huge sinkhole swallowing the Egyptian pyramids," and "Russian tanks appearing in Kyiv," which can be directly downloaded and shared. This type of AI-generated content, when combined with real geographic coordinates and the base map of Google Earth, has strong authenticity and can easily be mistaken for real satellite imagery.

Safety experts pointed out that during sensitive events such as wars or natural disasters, these highly realistic synthetic maps could be used to spread misinformation, misleading the public, media, and even investigators, posing new challenges for information verification.

Google stated that all AI-generated images are embedded with an invisible digital watermark and support authenticity verification through Gemini or Google Lens. However, the BBC test found that some verification mechanisms may still be bypassed, and some third-party detection tools are also unable to reliably identify AI-generated content.

The temporary suspension of the service reflects that as generative AI gradually enters high-trust information scenarios such as maps and remote sensing, how to enhance creative capabilities while preventing deepfakes and the spread of misinformation has become a key security issue that needs to be addressed in the deployment of AI products.

content_html_zh:
谷歌宣布暂停 Google Earth 中新推出的人工智能图像生成功能。 由于潜在的错误信息风险，该功能在推出后不到 48 小时就被暂时关闭。 该官员表示，将进一步加强安全措施。 此前，谷歌将图像生成模型 Nano Banana2 集成到 Google Earth 中，允许用户通过文本指令在真实卫星图像、航拍照片和 3D 地图上生成虚构场景。

据BBC测试，该功能可以生成“埃菲尔铁塔倒塌”、“吞噬埃及金字塔的巨大天坑”、“基辅出现俄罗斯坦克”等虚假场景，并可直接下载分享。 这类人工智能生成的内容，与真实的地理坐标和谷歌地球底图相结合，真实性很强，很容易被误认为是真实的卫星图像。

安全专家指出，在战争或自然灾害等敏感事件期间，这些高度真实的合成地图可能被用来传播错误信息，误导公众、媒体甚至调查人员，给信息验证带来新的挑战。

谷歌表示，所有人工智能生成的图像都嵌入了隐形数字水印，并支持通过 Gemini 或 Google Lens 进行真实性验证。 但BBC测试发现，部分验证机制仍可能被绕过，部分第三方检测工具也无法可靠识别AI生成的内容。

此次服务的暂时暂停反映出，随着生成式AI逐渐进入地图、遥感等高信任信息场景，如何在增强创意能力的同时防止深度造假和错误信息传播，成为AI产品部署中需要解决的关键安全问题。
